questions.question: The dimensional formula of pressure is
questions.explanation: Pressure = force / area. Force is [M L T⁻²] and area is [L²], so pressure is [M L T⁻²] / [L²] = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]. The same formula belongs to stress and Young's modulus.

questions.question: Two vectors have magnitudes 3 and 4 and are perpendicular to each other. The magnitude of their resultant is
questions.explanation: For perpendicular vectors, |A + B|² = |A|² + |B|² because the cross term 2|A||B|cos 90° is zero. So R = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5.

questions.question: A particle starts from rest. Its acceleration at time t seconds is a = 2t m/s². The distance travelled in the first 3 s is
questions.explanation: a = dv/dt = 2t. From rest, v = t². Then s = ∫ v dt from 0 to 3 = ∫ t² dt = [t³/3] from 0 to 3 = 9 m.

questions.question: A particle is projected from level ground with speed 20 m/s. Take g = 10 m/s². The maximum possible horizontal range, in metres, is
questions.explanation: R = u² sin 2θ / g. The maximum is at sin 2θ = 1, so θ = 45°. Rmax = u²/g = 400/10 = 40 m.

questions.question: Masses of 3 kg and 1 kg hang from a light inextensible string over a frictionless pulley. Take g = 10 m/s². The magnitude of acceleration of either mass, in m/s², is
questions.explanation: Atwood machine: a = (m1 − m2)g / (m1 + m2) = (3 − 1) × 10 / 4 = 5 m/s². The 3 kg mass descends.

questions.question: A 5 kg block is on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.2 and a horizontal force of 20 N is applied. Take g = 10 m/s². The acceleration, in m/s², is
questions.explanation: N = mg = 50 N. Kinetic friction = 0.2 × 50 = 10 N. Net force = 20 − 10 = 10 N. a = 10/5 = 2 m/s².

questions.question: A spring of force constant 100 N/m is compressed by 20 cm on a smooth horizontal table. A 1 kg block is released from rest against it. The maximum speed of the block is
questions.explanation: Spring energy becomes kinetic energy: (1/2)kx² = (1/2)mv². v = x √(k/m) = 0.20 × √100 = 2 m/s.

questions.question: A 2 kg body on a smooth horizontal surface speeds up from rest to 4 m/s under one horizontal force. The work done by that force is
questions.explanation: Work-energy theorem: work equals the gain in kinetic energy. ΔK = (1/2)(2)(4)² = 16 J.

questions.question: A particle moves in a circle of radius 5 m at a constant speed of 10 m/s. Its centripetal acceleration, in m/s², is
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration a = v²/r = 100/5 = 20 m/s², directed toward the centre. The tangential acceleration is zero because the speed is constant.

questions.question: A bullet of mass 0.01 kg moving at 200 m/s embeds in a stationary block of mass 1.99 kg. The kinetic energy lost in the collision, in joules, is
questions.explanation: Momentum conservation: 0.01 × 200 = 2.00 × V, so V = 1 m/s. Initial KE = (1/2)(0.01)(200)² = 200 J. Final KE = (1/2)(2)(1)² = 1 J. Loss = 199 J. The centre of mass of the combined system then moves at 1 m/s.

questions.question: A solid sphere and a thin spherical shell have the same mass and radius. They roll without slipping down the same incline from rest. The ratio of linear accelerations (solid sphere : shell) is
questions.explanation: a = g sinθ / (1 + I/MR²). Solid sphere: I/MR² = 2/5, so a_s = (5/7) g sinθ. Thin shell: I/MR² = 2/3, so a_shell = (3/5) g sinθ. Ratio = (5/7) / (3/5) = 25/21.

questions.question: A uniform disc of mass 2 kg and radius 0.4 m spins at 10 rad/s about its central axis. Its rotational kinetic energy, in joules, is
The acceleration due to gravity at a height equal to the Earth's radius R, above the surface, is
questions.explanation: g(h) = GM/(R + h)². At h = R, g' = GM/(2R)² = g/4. The approximation g(1 − 2h/R) is only for h much less than R.

questions.question: A wire is under a longitudinal stress of 2 × 10⁷ Pa and the corresponding strain is 10⁻³. The value of Young's modulus divided by 10¹⁰ Pa is
questions.explanation: Y = stress / strain = (2 × 10⁷) / 10⁻³ = 2 × 10¹⁰ Pa. Dividing by 10¹⁰ Pa gives 2.

questions.question: A small hole is opened 5 m below the free surface of a large open water tank. Take g = 10 m/s² and neglect viscosity. The speed of efflux, in m/s, is
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's equation between the free surface and the hole gives Torricelli's result v = √(2gh) = √(2 × 10 × 5) = 10 m/s.

questions.question: How much heat, in kilojoules, raises the temperature of 0.50 kg of water by 10 K? Take the specific heat of water as 4.2 kJ kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Q = mcΔT = 0.50 × 4.2 × 10 = 21 kJ. No phase change is involved, so latent heat is not added.

questions.question: A Carnot engine works between 600 K and 300 K. Its efficiency is
questions.explanation: η = 1 − T2/T1 = 1 − 300/600 = 1/2 = 50%. Both temperatures are already in kelvin.

questions.question: For a diatomic ideal gas at room temperature, with vibration not excited, the number of degrees of freedom is
questions.explanation: Translation contributes 3 and rotation of a diatomic molecule contributes 2. Vibration is frozen at room temperature, so f = 5. Then Cv = 5R/2 and γ = 7/5.

questions.question: A block of mass 1 kg is attached to a spring of force constant π² N/m on a smooth horizontal surface. The time period of small oscillations, in seconds, is
A progressive wave has frequency 250 Hz and wavelength 0.40 m. Its speed, in m/s, is
questions.explanation: Wave speed v = fλ = 250 × 0.40 = 100 m/s.

questions.question: Charges +q and −q are placed a distance 2a apart. The electric potential at the midpoint of the line joining them is
questions.explanation: The midpoint is a distance a from each charge. Potential is a scalar, so V = kq/a + k(−q)/a = 0. The electric field at that point is not zero.

questions.question: Two capacitors of 6 μF each are joined in series. The equivalent capacitance, in μF, is
A 12 V battery is connected to a 2 Ω resistor in series with the parallel combination of two 4 Ω resistors. The current drawn from the battery, in amperes, is
questions.explanation: Parallel pair: 1/Rp = 1/4 + 1/4, so Rp = 2 Ω. Total resistance = 2 + 2 = 4 Ω. I = 12/4 = 3 A.

questions.question: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with P = 2 Ω, Q = 4 Ω and R = 3 Ω. The fourth resistance S, in ohms, is
questions.explanation: Balance condition: P/Q = R/S. So 2/4 = 3/S, hence S = 6 Ω.

questions.question: A straight wire of length 0.4 m carries 5 A perpendicular to a uniform field of 0.5 T. The force on the wire, in newtons, is
questions.explanation: F = IlB sinθ with θ = 90°. F = 5 × 0.4 × 0.5 = 1 N.

questions.question: The magnetic susceptibility of which material is small and negative?
questions.explanation: Diamagnetic substances develop a weak moment opposite to the applied field, so χ is small and negative and μr is slightly less than 1. Paramagnetic χ is small and positive. Ferromagnetic χ is large and positive.

questions.question: A rod of length 2 m moves at 5 m/s perpendicular to its length and perpendicular to a uniform field of 0.2 T. The induced emf, in volts, is
questions.explanation: Motional emf = Blv = 0.2 × 2 × 5 = 2 V when B, l and v are mutually perpendicular.

questions.question: A series circuit has R = 3 Ω and inductive reactance 4 Ω, and no capacitor. The rms supply is 10 V. The rms current, in amperes, is
In vacuum, the ratio of the speed of gamma rays to the speed of radio waves is
questions.explanation: Every electromagnetic wave travels at c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s in vacuum, whatever its frequency. The ratio of the two speeds is 1. The speeds differ inside a material medium.

questions.question: An object is 30 cm to the left of a thin convex lens of focal length 10 cm. Distances to the left of the lens are negative. The image distance v, in cm, is
questions.explanation: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f with u = −30 cm and f = +10 cm. 1/v = 1/10 − 1/30 = 1/15, so v = +15 cm. The image is real and 15 cm to the right of the lens.

questions.question: A ray in glass of refractive index √2 meets a plane glass-air surface. The critical angle, in degrees, is
questions.explanation: sin C = 1/μ = 1/√2, so C = 45°. Incidence in glass beyond this angle gives total internal reflection.

questions.question: Light of wavelength 310 nm is incident on a metal of work function 2.0 eV. Take hc = 1240 eV·nm. The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons, in eV, is
questions.explanation: Photon energy = 1240/310 = 4.0 eV. Kmax = hf − φ = 4.0 − 2.0 = 2.0 eV.

questions.question: In Bohr's model of hydrogen, the ratio of the radius of the n = 2 orbit to the radius of the n = 1 orbit is
The half-life of a sample is 3 hours. The time, in hours, in which its activity falls to 1/16 of the initial activity is
questions.explanation: (1/2)^n = 1/16 gives n = 4 half-lives. t = 4 × 3 = 12 hours. Activity and the number of nuclei fall by the same factor.

questions.question: Forward bias of a p-n junction diode
questions.explanation: Forward bias applies a voltage that opposes the built-in potential. The barrier height falls and the depletion layer becomes thinner, so majority carriers cross the junction more easily.
